description: Dependency-free .NET 8 APIs for URIs, encoding, DNS, IP addresses, HTTP messages and content, TCP streams, and cookies.
executionSupportMessage: Compatible with the built-in .NET 10 C# runner; authored against .NET 8.

actionDescriptions.Add: Adds a value, item, header, or contribution to an existing object.
actionDescriptions.Build: Constructs a value or operation from smaller pieces.
actionDescriptions.Create: Constructs a new object, resource, or language structure.
actionDescriptions.Decode: Converts an encoded representation back into its original form.
actionDescriptions.Encode: Converts data into a representation suitable for storage or transport.
actionDescriptions.Get: Retrieves information without intentionally changing the source.
actionDescriptions.Parse: Interprets text or bytes as a structured value.
actionDescriptions.Read: Reads text, bytes, messages, or values from a source.
actionDescriptions.Resolve: Translates a name or identifier into a concrete runtime or network value.
actionDescriptions.Send: Transmits a request, message, or bytes to another component.
actionDescriptions.Write: Writes text, bytes, messages, or values to a destination.

objectDescriptions.Host name: A host name is a DNS label or fully qualified name resolved to one or more network addresses.
objectDescriptions.HTML text: HTML text is character data intended for a markup document; safe encoding depends on its exact HTML context.
objectDescriptions.HTTP content: HttpContent represents an HTTP request or response body plus its content headers.
objectDescriptions.HTTP cookie: An HTTP cookie is a small name-value record scoped by host, path, security, expiry, and related request rules.
objectDescriptions.HTTP form content: Form URL-encoded content represents key-value fields using the application/x-www-form-urlencoded media type.
objectDescriptions.HTTP header: An HTTP header is a named metadata field associated with a request, response, or content body.
objectDescriptions.HTTP JSON content: HTTP JSON content is an HTTP body encoded as JSON and described by content headers.
objectDescriptions.HTTP JSON request: An HTTP JSON request combines a method and URI with a JSON-serialized request body.
objectDescriptions.HTTP request: An HttpRequestMessage describes one outbound HTTP operation, including its method, URI, headers, content, and version policy.
objectDescriptions.HTTP stream: An HTTP stream exposes response-body bytes incrementally rather than buffering the entire body.
objectDescriptions.IP address: An IPAddress represents an IPv4 or IPv6 network address without DNS naming or transport-port information.
objectDescriptions.TCP connection: A TCP connection is a reliable ordered byte stream between a local and remote network endpoint.
objectDescriptions.TCP stream: A NetworkStream reads and writes bytes through a connected stream-oriented socket.
objectDescriptions.URI: A URI is a structured identifier containing components such as scheme, authority, path, query, and fragment.
objectDescriptions.URL component: A URL component is one structural portion of a URL whose reserved characters require context-appropriate encoding.

commands.name: Uri.TryCreate
commands.description: Try to parse and validate a URI.
commands.definition: Attempts to create a Uri with the requested relative or absolute form and returns false instead of throwing when the text is not valid for that form.
commands.template: var valid = Uri.TryCreate({text}, {uriKind}, out var uri);

examples.title: Require an HTTPS address
examples.explanation: Parsing and the explicit scheme check together reject relative and non-HTTPS values.

commands.name: UriBuilder.Create
commands.description: Build or modify a URI by components.
commands.definition: UriBuilder exposes scheme, host, port, path, query, and fragment as mutable components and produces a correctly assembled Uri.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The query text without a leading question mark.

examples.title: Compose an API endpoint
examples.explanation: UriBuilder adds separators between the scheme, host, path, and query components.

commands.name: WebUtility.UrlEncode
commands.description: Percent-encode text for use in a URL component.
commands.definition: Converts characters that are unsafe in a URL component into percent-encoded UTF-8 bytes. It does not by itself assemble or validate a complete URI.

examples.title: Encode a query value
examples.explanation: Spaces, the hash sign, and ampersand are encoded so they remain part of the q value.

commands.name: WebUtility.UrlDecode
commands.description: Decode percent-encoded URL component text.
commands.definition: Replaces percent-encoded byte sequences with their decoded characters and converts plus signs according to form-style URL encoding rules.

examples.title: Decode a query value
examples.code:
var decoded = WebUtility.UrlDecode("C%23+streams+%26+files");
Console.WriteLine(decoded);
examples.explanation: The encoded sequence becomes readable C# streams & files text.

commands.name: WebUtility.HtmlEncode
commands.description: Encode text for safe placement in HTML text content.
commands.definition: Replaces characters with special HTML meaning with entity references. Context-specific encoding is still required for attributes, scripts, styles, and URLs.

examples.title: Encode a display label
examples.code:
var encoded = WebUtility.HtmlEncode(" & guests"); Console.WriteLine($"

{encoded}

");
examples.explanation: Angle brackets and the ampersand are represented as text rather than being interpreted as markup.

commands.name: WebUtility.HtmlDecode
commands.description: Decode HTML entity references into text.
commands.definition: Converts recognized named and numeric HTML entities back to their character values. Decoding does not sanitize untrusted markup.

examples.title: Restore encoded display text
examples.explanation: Entity references become literal characters in the returned .NET string.

commands.name: Dns.GetHostAddressesAsync
commands.description: Resolve a DNS host name to IP addresses asynchronously.
commands.definition: Queries configured name-resolution services and returns the IPv4 and/or IPv6 addresses associated with a host name.

parameters.name: hostName
parameters.description: The DNS host name to resolve.

examples.title: Resolve a service host
examples.explanation: The result may contain several IPv4 and IPv6 addresses and can change across networks or calls.

commands.name: Dns.GetHostEntryAsync
commands.description: Resolve a host and retrieve canonical name information.
commands.definition: Returns an IPHostEntry containing the canonical host name, aliases, and resolved IP addresses available from the configured resolver.

parameters.name: hostName
parameters.description: The DNS name or textual IP address.

examples.title: Inspect a host entry
examples.explanation: The resolver returns canonical naming and every address it associates with localhost.

commands.name: IPAddress.TryParse
commands.description: Try to parse IPv4 or IPv6 address text.
commands.definition: Attempts to interpret text as an IPAddress and returns false instead of throwing when the representation is invalid.
commands.template: var valid = IPAddress.TryParse({text}, out var address);

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The candidate IPv4 or IPv6 text.

examples.title: Validate a literal address
examples.explanation: The parsed value reports its address family without requiring DNS.

commands.name: HttpClient.GetStreamAsync
commands.description: Open an HTTP response body as a readable stream.
commands.definition: Sends a GET request, ensures a successful status, and returns the response body stream without first buffering the entire content.

parameters.name: requestUri
parameters.description: The absolute or base-relative request URI.

examples.title: Stream an HTTP body into a file
examples.explanation: The body is copied incrementally instead of being materialized as one string or byte array.

commands.name: HttpClient.PutAsJsonAsync
commands.description: Send a JSON-encoded HTTP PUT request.
commands.definition: Serializes a value as JSON, sends it in an HTTP PUT request, and returns the response. The caller remains responsible for status handling and HttpClient lifetime.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value to serialize as JSON.

examples.title: Replace an API resource
examples.explanation: The anonymous object becomes a JSON request body; production code should validate the returned status.

commands.name: HttpClient.DeleteAsync
commands.description: Send an HTTP DELETE request.
commands.definition: Sends a DELETE request to the selected URI and returns the complete response metadata and content handle.

examples.title: Delete an API resource
examples.explanation: EnsureSuccessStatusCode turns a non-success response into an exception after the request completes.

commands.name: HttpContent.ReadAsStringAsync
commands.description: Read an HTTP content body as text.
commands.definition: Buffers the content bytes, selects an encoding from the content headers when available, and returns the decoded string.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: An HttpContent response or request body.

examples.title: Inspect an unsuccessful response body
examples.explanation: The content is decoded independently of whether the HTTP status represents success.

commands.name: HttpContent.ReadFromJsonAsync<T>
commands.description: Deserialize an HTTP content body from JSON.
commands.definition: Reads content as a JSON document and deserializes it into the requested .NET type using web-oriented serializer defaults unless options are supplied.

examples.title: Read a JSON dictionary
examples.explanation: The in-memory JSON content is deserialized into a strongly typed dictionary.

commands.name: HttpRequestMessage.Create
commands.description: Create a configurable HTTP request message.
commands.definition: Combines an HTTP method, URI, headers, options, version policy, and optional content into a message that HttpClient.SendAsync can transmit.

examples.title: Create a conditional GET request
examples.explanation: A request object allows conditional headers to be configured before sending.

commands.name: HttpHeaders.TryAddWithoutValidation
commands.description: Try to add a raw HTTP header value.
commands.definition: Adds a header without parsing the value against the known header grammar. It should be reserved for compatibility cases; untrusted values still require policy and injection safeguards.

examples.title: Add a vendor compatibility header
examples.explanation: The custom header is accepted without a registered parser; standard strongly typed header properties remain preferable.

commands.name: FormUrlEncodedContent.Create
commands.description: Create an application/x-www-form-urlencoded HTTP body.
commands.definition: Encodes key-value pairs using HTML form URL-encoding rules and exposes them as HttpContent with the appropriate media type.

examples.title: Build a form request body
examples.explanation: Keys and values are percent-encoded and joined into a standard form body.

commands.name: TcpClient.ConnectAsync
commands.description: Asynchronously connect a TCP client to a remote endpoint.
commands.definition: Resolves the host when necessary and attempts a TCP connection to the requested port, honoring an optional cancellation token.

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: A DNS name or textual IP address.

examples.title: Connect to a local ephemeral listener
examples.explanation: An ephemeral loopback listener verifies the client connection without contacting an external service.

commands.name: NetworkStream.WriteAsync
commands.description: Asynchronously write bytes to a connected network stream.
commands.definition: Writes bytes to the underlying connected socket and completes after the supplied buffer has been accepted for transmission or an error occurs.

examples.title: Exchange a loopback message
examples.explanation: The local client writes four bytes and the accepted server connection reads exactly those bytes.

commands.name: CookieContainer.Add
commands.description: Store a cookie for a URI.
commands.definition: Adds a Cookie under a URI-derived domain and path scope. CookieContainer enforces capacity and cookie-format rules.

parameters.name: uri
parameters.description: The URI that supplies cookie scope.

examples.title: Store a scoped preference cookie
examples.explanation: The cookie is scoped to the URI's host and default path rules.

commands.name: CookieContainer.GetCookies
commands.description: Get cookies applicable to a URI.
commands.definition: Returns the non-expired cookies whose domain, path, port, and secure rules allow them to be sent to the selected URI.

parameters.name: uri
parameters.description: The request URI used for cookie matching.

examples.title: Inspect cookies for one path
examples.explanation: Only cookies applicable to the requested host, path, and scheme are returned.
